s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with migration to the right lower quadrant
salient_findings: Abdominal pain migrating from the umbilicus to the right lower quadrant
Voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant
Leukocytosis with a white-cell count of 15,600/mL
key_facts: 58-year-old man presented with abdominal pain
Pain began around the umbilicus 2 days prior to presentation
Pain migrated to the right lower quadrant
No prior abdominal surgeries or systemic disease
Afebrile on examination
Heart rate was 86 bpm
Blood pressure was 130/95 mmHg
Abdominal examination showed minimal tenderness elsewhere
Laboratory tests revealed a white-cell count of 15,600/mL
Hemoglobin was 14.2 g/dL
Platelet count was 126,000/mL
Plain abdominal X-rays demonstrated several air-fluid levels without free air under the diaphragm

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Migratory periumbilical to right lower quadrant pain and leukocytosis

shortlist.label: Plastron appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Ultrasound findings compatible with this condition

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of right lower quadrant pain and elevated white-cell count

shortlist.label: Small intestinal perforation
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of air-fluid levels on abdominal X-rays

shortlist.label: Diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of abdominal pain and elevated white-cell count

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including migratory pain from the umbilicus to the right lower quadrant, elevated white-cell count, and ultrasound findings, are consistent with acute appendicitis.

rejected.label: Plastron appendicitis
rejected.why: While ultrasound suggested plastron appendicitis, the overall clinical presentation and laboratory findings more strongly support acute appendicitis.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
rejected.why: There is no specific indication of Meckel's diverticulum, such as gastrointestinal bleeding or a history suggestive of diverticulum complications.

rejected.label: Small intestinal perforation
rejected.why: The absence of free air under the diaphragm on plain abdominal X-rays makes perforation less likely.

rejected.label: Diverticulitis
rejected.why: The patient's age and presentation are not typical for diverticulitis, which usually occurs in older adults with left lower quadrant pain.
